Pep Guardiola on Japan's first-half performance against Brazil:

🗣️ “I don't know what Hajime Moriyasu has done with this Japanese team, but what I'm watching is extraordinary. People spent weeks talking about Brazil's stars, yet for forty-five minutes it's Japan who have looked like the real giants on this pitch.”

“Brazil have world-class players in every position. Alisson, Marquinhos, Gabriel, Casemiro, Bruno Guimarães, Vinícius Júnior... these are names that strike fear across world football. But today, Japan have completely ignored reputations and played with courage, intelligence and absolute belief.”

“Nakamura, Kamada, Sano and Doan have been fearless. Every attack looks dangerous, every press is coordinated, and every player is fighting as if this is the biggest moment of their lives. That mentality is worth more than any transfer fee.”

“What impresses me most is the discipline. Tomiyasu, Taniguchi and Ito have made Brazil's attack look ordinary. When you can silence players like Vinícius Júnior and Matheus Cunha on the biggest stage, you're doing something very special.”

“This is why football is the greatest sport in the world. Expensive squads don't win matches teams do. Right now Japan look hungrier, sharper and mentally stronger than Brazil.”

“If Brazil don't change something immediately, this could become one of the biggest World Cup shocks we've seen in years. Japan aren't just competing anymore... they're making Brazil suffer.”

ペップ・グアルディオラがブラジル戦の日本代表前半のパフォーマンスについて語る：

🗣️ 「森保一監督がこの日本チームに何をしたのか分からないが、私が見ているものは並外れている。人々は何週間もブラジルのスター選手について話していたが、45分間、ピッチ上の真の巨人のように見えたのは日本だ。」

「ブラジルはあらゆるポジションにワールドクラスの選手がいる。アリソン、マルキーニョス、ガブリエル、カゼミーロ、ブルーノ・ギマランイス、ヴィニシウス・ジュニオール...これらは世界のサッカーに恐怖をもたらす名前だ。しかし今日、日本は名声など完全に無視し、勇気、知性、そして絶対的な信念を持ってプレーした。」

「中村、鎌田、佐野、堂安は恐れることなくプレーした。どの攻撃も危険に見え、どのプレスも連携されており、全ての選手が人生最大の瞬間のために戦っているかのようだ。そのメンタリティはどんな移籍金よりも価値がある。」

「私が最も感銘を受けたのは規律だ。冨安、谷口、伊藤はブラジルの攻撃を平凡に見せた。ヴィニシウス・ジュニオールやマテウス・クーニャのような選手を大舞台で沈黙させられるとき、それは非常に特別なことをしている証拠だ。」

「これがサッカーが世界最高のスポーツである理由だ。高価な選手を揃えたチームが試合に勝つのではなく、チームが勝つのだ。今、日本はブラジルよりもハングリーで、シャープで、精神的に強い。」

「もしブラジルがすぐに何かを変えなければ、これはここ数年で最大のワールドカップの番狂わせの一つになるかもしれない。日本はもはや競い合っているだけではない…ブラジルを苦しめているのだ。」

🚨🇯🇵Rio Ferdinand Praises Japan’s Coach After Brave World Cup Exit

“I have to give enormous credit to Japan and especially to their coach. Before this tournament, almost every prediction had Brazil winning comfortably. Most people expected Japan to defend deep, concede possession and eventually get overwhelmed. Instead, they made one of the greatest football nations in history fight until the very last moments.”

“What surprised me most throughout this World Cup wasn’t just the results—it was the discipline. Every player understood his role. Their defensive shape was outstanding, their pressing was organised, and whenever they had the ball, they attacked with courage instead of fear. That’s coaching. That’s hours on the training ground turning a group of good players into a genuine team.”

“Against Brazil they never looked intimidated. They scored first, frustrated Brazil for long spells, and every time Brazil thought they had found a way through, Japan responded with incredible determination. They were only minutes away from taking one of the biggest scalps in World Cup history.”

“It’s heartbreaking that a late goal from Martinelli is what sends them home. Football can be brutally cruel. One moment separates celebration from elimination. But Japan shouldn’t be remembered for losing this match—they should be remembered for making Brazil struggle far more than anyone expected.”

“This tournament has changed the way people see Japanese football. Their coach deserves enormous praise because he built a team with identity, discipline and belief. They may be out of the competition, but they’ve earned something that lasts much longer than a place in the next round: the respect of the entire football world.”

🗣️ “This is the cruelest side of football. Japan gave everything they had for ninety-five minutes, pushed one of the greatest football nations in history to the edge, and yet they're the team going home. That's a heartbreak that will stay with those players forever.”

“They didn't lose because they lacked courage. They didn't lose because they stopped believing. They lost because against teams like Brazil, one single moment is enough to destroy ninety minutes of extraordinary football.”

“I hope these players don't let this defeat define them. They have earned the respect of the entire football world. They came here as underdogs, but they leave as a team every nation will remember.”

“The tears you're seeing tonight are not tears of failure they're the tears of players who gave absolutely everything for their country. Sometimes football can be incredibly unfair, and this is one of those nights that will hurt for a very long time.”

“Brazil survive, but Japan leave with their heads held high. Sometimes football doesn't reward the team that captures hearts it rewards the team that takes its final chance. That's why this game is so beautiful... and so brutally unforgiving.”

ティエリ・アンリが語る、ブラジルに敗れてFIFAワールドカップから敗退した日本について：

🗣️ 「これがフットボールの最も残酷な側面だ。日本は95分間、持てる力の全てを出し切り、史上最高のサッカー大国の一つを土壇場まで追い詰めた。それでも彼らが帰路につくチームだ。それは選手たちの中に永遠に残るであろう、心の痛みだ。」

「彼らは勇気がなかったから負けたのではない。信じることをやめたから負けたのでもない。ブラジルのようなチームを相手にすれば、たった一つの瞬間に90分間の素晴らしいサッカーが台無しになるから負けたのだ。」

「この敗北が彼らを定義するものでないことを願う。彼らはサッカー界全体の尊敬を勝ち取った。彼らはここでは下馬評の低いチームだったが、全ての国が記憶するチームとして去っていく。」

「今夜見ている涙は失敗の涙ではない、国のために全てを捧げた選手たちの涙だ。時としてフットボールは信じられないほど不公平であり、今夜は長く心に刻まれるであろう夜の一つだ。」

「ブラジルは生き残ったが、日本は胸を張って去る。フットボールは時に心を掴んだチームに報いるのではなく、最後のチャンスをものにしたチームに報いる。だからこそこのゲームは美しく…そして残酷なまでに容赦ないのだ。」

Pep Guardiola on Japan’s dominant 4–0 victory over Tunisia at the World Cup:

“When you perform at this level consistently, you stop being a surprise. You become a team that everyone must respect.

“Before the tournament, everyone was speaking about the usual big nations. Meanwhile, Japan were quietly building a team with identity, discipline, and courage.

“The most dangerous thing about this team is their mentality. Even at 3–0 or 4–0, they continue pressing, continue running, and continue searching for more goals. They never stop.

“Football does not care about history or reputation. It cares about what you do on the pitch. Right now, Japan are showing a level that puts them among the strongest teams in this tournament.

“If I were managing one of the traditional powerhouses, Japan would be one of the teams I would least want to face. They are organised, fearless, and improving with every match.

“And that is how great World Cup stories are written.”

“For many years, people questioned whether Asian teams could consistently compete with the traditional football powers. Japan are answering that question in the strongest way possible.”

“This achievement will inspire millions of young players across Asia. There will be children watching this performance and believing that they too can dream of reaching the highest level.”

Wesley Sneijder on Japan's dominant 4-0 victory over Tunisia at the World Cup:

🗣️ “People might look at the Netherlands drawing 2-2 with Japan earlier in the tournament and only focus on the result. But after watching them destroy Tunisia 4-0, I can tell you that draw looks more impressive with every passing day.”

“When we faced Japan, you could immediately feel how organized they were. They never stopped running, never stopped pressing, and never gave you a second to relax on the ball.”

“A lot of teams have talented players, but Japan have something even more dangerous right now complete belief. Every player understands his role and every player is willing to sacrifice for the team.”

“This 4-0 victory wasn't just a win. It was a statement to the rest of the World Cup. Tunisia simply could not live with the speed, movement, and intensity that Japan brought to the match.”

“What impressed me most is that Japan don't play like outsiders anymore. They play like a team that genuinely believes it belongs among the best nations in the tournament.”

“When the Netherlands played them, there were moments where they caused us serious problems. They were fearless. They attacked with confidence and defended with incredible discipline.”

“That's why I'm not surprised by what happened against Tunisia. The signs were already there. Japan have been building towards a performance like this.”

“If they continue playing with this level of confidence and organization, they will become one of the most dangerous teams in the knockout rounds. Nobody will be excited to face them.”

“Before the tournament started, people talked about Japan as a dark horse. After performances like this, they're forcing people to have a completely different conversation.”

“And trust me, after seeing them up close and watching them dismantle Tunisia 4-0, I can say with confidence that Japan are becoming one of the teams capable of shocking the entire football world.”
